messages:
devon: heads up — telemetry just flagged a 3x spike in ECC corrected errors and a small XID bump on eu-west-1 gpu pool (p4d-like). seeing it across ~6 racks, not isolated. link: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/gpu/eu-west1-ecc?orgId=1 :eyes:

oncall-bot: incident created: GPU_ERR_SURGE-EU-WEST-1 #2167890123

rachel: thanks. can you paste the prom query you used? want to audit the window and model distribution

devon: query was `sum by (instance, gpu_model) (increase(gpu_ecc_corrected_total[30m]))` then ranked. also crosschecked `increase(gpu_xid_errors_total[1h])` — XID numbers small but correlated with a couple of nodes that show ECC rising steadily

chris: do we have any recent kernel/driver firmware changes deployed to eu-west? last kernel roll was 2165000000 but driver firmware push was staged only to us-west

devon: no recent firmware pushes here. config shows older driver on those racks (nv-510.85). suspected flaky cards?

lee: capacity question — if we start preemptive drains/replacements how much spare do we have in eu-west? last reserve is ~12% but baseline load is higher during EMEA business hours

rachel: prefer a cautious plan: 1) quiesce scheduling to soft-drain affected nodes (cordon & gentle evict), 2) run `gpu-health-check` burn-in on swapped VM, 3) if ECC rate doesn't drop after burnin -> mark for replacement. threshold: >100 corrected errs/hour for 2 consecutive windows OR any XID_UNCORRECTABLE >0

chris: +1 on burn-in. can we do an automated canary for firmware bump on a single rack? run firmware on 1 host with observed issues and monitor 6h trend before wider push

devon: we can. but two operational constraints: 1) avoid draining >5% of region GPUs within 4h, 2) avoid cross-zone impact — keep replacements zonal unless we need to burst to other regions

siva: ops question — do we prefer hot-swap (replace card in place) or reprovision node + reprovision? hot-swap takes rack tech time ~45m, reprovisioning a new node from pool is ~25m but costs some compute spin-up. reprovision seems faster for large batches

lee: cost tradeoff: reprovisioning will spike short-term cloud costs if we spin new reserved GPUs. propose we throttle to 3 nodes/hr unless emergency

rachel: agreed. add automatic throttle: if active replacements in region >=3 -> pause automated replacements and escalate to oncall. fallback: if XID_UNCORRECTABLE seen mark immediate emergency replacement and notify oncall

infra-bot: action created: /fleet drain set soft gpu-rack-07 --reason "ECC surge" --max-concurrent 3

chris: one more metric tweak: capture `gpu_ecc_rate_normalized = increase(gpu_ecc_corrected_total[1h]) / (minutes_active)` and alert on slope > 0.5 errors/minute over 2h to catch slow risers

devon: updating dashboard now and will push a temporary alert rule to paging: `alert: GPU_ECC_SLOW_RISE` expr: `increase(gpu_ecc_corrected_total[2h]) > 600` for eu-west1 targets

siva: we'll need a short playbook snippet for oncall: steps to verify, commands, and how to trigger reprovision. draft below:
- check grafana link and `sum by (instance) (increase(gpu_ecc_corrected_total[30m]))`
- `ssh ops@node` run `/usr/local/bin/gpu-health-check --burnin 30m`
- if fail -> mark node `fleetctl mark bad --node node-id` then `fleetctl reprovision --node node-id --type replacement-sku`
- if multiple nodes -> coordinate with capacity (lee)

rachel: nice. add `kubectl cordon <node>` + `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=120` to soft-drain step and mention `--force` only for emergency

chris: also capture firmware/kernel mapping in the incident note so we can correlate later: `node-exporter` labels GPU driver/kernel/firmware hashes. pull those into the incident playbook

devon: I'll kick off a 1-rack firmware canary tonight at 23:00 UTC and a reprovision window for up to 2 nodes if burn-in fails. tagging @lee for capacity approval

lee: approved for up to 2 reprovisions overnight. keep it within the 3 node/hr throttle. notify infra channel before starting

oncall-bot: scheduled action: firmware-canary-eu-west-1 @ 2026-03-19T23:00:00Z — id: fc-2167890123

rachel: after canary, if trend improves we'll backfill a batch replace schedule over 7 days limited to 1 rack/day. if not, escalate to hardware vendor for warranty replacement

devon: will post short postmortem in #eng-platform after completion with kernel/driver mapping and final counts. tracking ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/GPU-REPLACE-2167

chris: reminder: update `infra-monitoring` docs with new thresholds and the `GPU_ECC_SLOW_RISE` rule once validated

siva: +1. I'll update the oncall runbook and add a checklist entry for `verify NVLINK/cooling metrics` before replacement — sometimes thermal cycling causes spurious ECC

devon: thanks all — starting dashboard patch and will ping before canary start. :wave:
